title: RAG for VPs of AI: Jerry Liu
talk_summary: Jerry Liu of LlamaIndex gives a vendor overview of RAG components (parsing, chunking, indexing, reranking) and takes audience questions on data quality, privacy, versioning, and long-context vs retrieval. The only transferable mechanisms are about data/context quality and eval-driven tuning, not agent orchestration or cost control.

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the parse step is the dominant failure source: naive PDF parsers collapse tables/numbers and cause downstream hallucination, so they lay text out spatially aligned before chunking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you use like a very naive parser like a baseline PDF parser um it's going to like collapse the text and numbers

takeaways.what_they_do: They say chunk size and pipeline parameters are 'fuzzy' and cannot be set without an end-to-end eval dataset and rigorous testing flow, unlike deterministic ETL.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's really hard to tell what the chunk size you need to set is without having an eval data set

takeaways.what_they_do: For diverse data sources they run separate pipelines per source type and combine results with a reranking layer at the top rather than one uniform pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just have to like combine them together and rerank them right and and have some reranking layer

takeaways.what_they_do: They predict intra-page chunking fades as context windows grow, indexing whole self-contained documents instead, but note full-corpus stuffing stays cost-prohibitive and opaque.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as context Windows get bigger chunk sizes can also get bigger
